title: Abaye bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He and his brother Rav Chanina were Rabbah’s students: Pesachim 34a has them studying Terumot in Rabbah’s school when Rava bar Matnu met them and asked what they were learning in their master’s Terumot teaching. Abaye was something like their colleague, sitting with them in Eruvin 62a and 89a.

Hyman says that they are mentioned everywhere together with the formula “both of them say”: Berakhot 29b; Shabbat 86b; Eruvin 62a, 87b and 89a; Yevamot 36a and 108a; Bava Batra 87b; and Bekhorot 42b. The supplied Keritot locator is ס.; a matching passage at Keritot 20a reads Ami bar Avin, for which Hyman proposes Abaye. In Megillah 7b they exchange Purim meals—to fulfill sending portions, or, according to Rashi, one eats with the other one year and the arrangement is reversed the next.

notes.text: The ordinary Abaye mentioned as their colleague is distinct from the subject Abaye bar Avin. The supplied Keritot ס. would be folio 60, which does not resolve to an ordinary folio of that tractate; it remains a source question.
The checked Megillah calls the brother Rabbi Chanina; Hyman supplies Rav Chanina, which is retained.

The saved William Davidson vocalized text of Keritot 20a explicitly has Ami bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin “both saying.” This is a matching passage for Hyman’s proposed Ami-to-Abaye correction. The supplied ס. locator remains recorded as a discrepancy; the digital match does not prove whether it arose in the print or in transcription.
